premise: What if humans discovered the real anti-aging molecule, and it became as easy and common as having a phone?
title:
WHAT IF AGING
WAS AN APP?

lines.text: What if the cure for aging fit in your pocket, like a phone?
Scientists already reversed signs of aging in mice, by switching on four special genes.

facts.claim: Partial reprogramming with the four Yamanaka factors countered signs of aging in mice.
facts.quote: the expression of four genes known as the Yamanaka factors
facts.quote2: countering signs of aging and increasing the animals’ lifespan by 30 percent

lines.text: A drug called rapamycin made old mice live longer. Now imagine it worked on us.

facts.claim: Rapamycin fed late in life extended median and maximal lifespan of mice.
facts.quote: rapamycin, an inhibitor of the mTOR pathway, extends median and maximal lifespan of both male and female mice

lines.text: One tap a day. All eight billion of us, staying young.

facts.claim: World population reached 8 billion on 15 November 2022.
facts.quote: the world’s population reached 8 billion people

lines.text: Cities overflow. Towers stack up into the clouds.
Your great great great grandma looks twenty five, and she still wants the window seat.
Retirement? Gone. Your first job could last a hundred and fifty years.
The oldest person ever reached one hundred twenty two. Now that's just middle age.

facts.claim: Jeanne Calment died at 122 years and 164 days, the oldest verified person.

lines.text: Then one morning, every phone on Earth buzzes at once. Your free trial has ended.
